clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The operative paragraph approves the amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry and modifies the previous approval to include approval of the code in its entirety as amended, effective fourteen days after August 21, 1934 absent a contrary order, none of which is held. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6828 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6828-approving-amendments-code-fair-competition-for-the-cotton-garment.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (62db0994c914...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-51, captured 2025-12-12T23:26:13Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6828—Approving Amendments to Code of Fair Competition For the Cotton Garment Industry' and whose date is 1934-08-21; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('August 21, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6828—Approving Amendments to Code of Fair Competition For the Cotton Garment Industry', 1934-08-21) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 589: 'Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry approved.'). The WPA list says the order approves amendments to the Cotton Garment Code (page 589). EO 6828 (August 21, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) adopts the Administrator's report on hearings held on amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry and orders 'that the said amendments be and they are hereby approved, and that a previous order of approval of said Code is hereby modified to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended, such approval to take effect fourteen (14) days from the date hereof' unless good cause to the contrary were shown to the Administrator before then and a subsequent order issued. Legal reading: one section 3(a) approval of amendments with a suspensive proviso. The proviso could have prevented the approval from taking effect on September 4, 1934 only through a subsequent order issued within the fourteen days; no held order concerning the Cotton Garment code issued between August 21 and September 4, 1934, and both EO 6861 and EO 6871 recite that EO 6828 'approved' the amendments, so the approval is treated as having taken effect on its terms. The approval has no period of its own and ends with the repeal on 1935-06-14. EO 6861 (September 28, 1934) stayed the effective date of the amendments to Articles III and IV, which by their terms were not to take effect until October 1, 1934, up to and including October 15, 1934; EO 6871 (October 12, 1934) revoked that stay's first paragraph, stayed the same amendments 'to and including December 1, 1934, after which date said amendments shall be in full force and effect', continued the committee and set further reports. Those are postponements of the effective date of part of what this order approved, not cancellations of the approval, and the amendments were to be in force after December 1, 1934; they are described here and are not cited as later events because the order's dossier carries no evidence record for them.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. Acts done while the amendments to Articles III and IV were stayed, and acts done under the other amendments between September 4, 1934 and the repeal, are accrued effects.
